scope: Opt-in diagnostic-only actual-successor census for code16 terminal single JZ/JNZ fallbacks; no linked guest execution
decision: No-go for a narrow Jcc-to-current-block performance slice: only 6.40% of terminal single-Jcc calls have a ready same-page successor under the present decoder, and only 1.49% are register-only. Broaden opcode, stack and store coverage and reduce block-entry cost first.
limits: These are dispatcher-call and post-step syntactic readiness counts, not distinct static branches or a linked executor's retired instruction count. The current decoder rejects a one-instruction successor, so 877,964 such refusals may conceal recursive graph opportunities; their forms were not classified. A post-step proof does not establish that the previous chip-event budget could have admitted a linked successor. Diagnostic timing includes millions of extra decode/proof probes. Commercial media and raw reports remain private.
